question: Two coherent sources produce interference at a point. The maximum and minimum intensities observed are in the ratio $9:1$. Obtain the ratio of the intensities of the two sources. Also explain why the same calculation cannot be applied to incoherent sources.

options.A: For coherent waves, $I_{max}=(\sqrt{I_1}+\sqrt{I_2})^2$ and $I_{min}=(\sqrt{I_1}-\sqrt{I_2})^2$. From $I_{max}:I_{min}=9:1$, $\dfrac{\sqrt{I_1}+\sqrt{I_2}}{\sqrt{I_1}-\sqrt{I_2}}=3$, giving $\sqrt{I_1}=2\sqrt{I_2}$ and hence $I_1:I_2=4:1$. This calculation requires coherent sources, because only a fixed phase difference produces stable maximum and minimum intensities; incoherent sources have random phase and no stable fringes.
options.B: The source intensity ratio is $9:1$. The same result applies to incoherent sources because phase does not affect intensity.
options.C: The source intensity ratio is $3:1$. Incoherent sources give the same stable maximum and minimum intensities.
options.D: The source intensity ratio is $1:4$. The calculation applies to incoherent waves because their phase difference is fixed.
